steps.title: Audience Complicity
steps.body: Dramatic irony makes the audience feel involved - we know secrets, we anticipate outcomes, we're emotionally invested.

steps.title: Why Off-Stage?
steps.body: Some violence too extreme for stage; imagination more powerful; focuses on psychological aftermath rather than physical act.

steps.title: Banquo as Foil
steps.body: He shows what Macbeth could have been - the alternative path. His murder marks Macbeth's descent into true tyranny.

steps.title: Dramatic Techniques Strategy
steps.body: Focus on what the AUDIENCE experiences. Ask: "What does the audience know that characters don't? What can the audience see that characters can't? How does Shakespeare control what we feel and when?" Analyse dramatic irony, soliloquies, entrances/exits, and on-stage vs off-stage action. Always link technique to audience effect.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What is dramatic irony and give an example from "Macbeth". | How does Shakespeare use the supernatural to create tension? | What is the function of Banquo as a foil to Macbeth?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Dramatic irony is when the audience knows more than characters. Example: Duncan praises Macbeth's loyalty while we know he plans murder. Creates tension and makes audience complicit. | Witches establish evil from the opening; prophecies drive plot; ambiguity creates irony; ghost and hallucinations show psychological horror. Supernatural creates atmosphere and motivates action. | Banquo contrasts Macbeth - both receive prophecies, but Banquo resists temptation. He shows what Macbeth could have been. His murder marks Macbeth's descent into tyranny.
